output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation, not a fault in v4.18. Over the prior 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% with a normal-band upper edge of 0.482%. Weeks hit 0.51%, 0.47% and 0.45% with no fault found, and 0.41% is inside the band. The dashboard count matches raw logs, so it is not a counting artefact. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Booking completion was flat and there were no complaints. The rollout comparison that points at v4.18 is misleading. New pods start with cold caches and time out against the replica in every rollout. That includes an unchanged config-only redeploy and the four earlier releases, at 0.47–0.58% against 0.29–0.33% on old pods. It adds only 10–20 errors. So I would not roll back, and I would not mute the alerts. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to next week. If next week is above the band or the page fires, open an incident. The replica host change and partner-sync month-end traffic are not ruled out, but nothing here needs action. Confidence is fairly high but not complete.
